{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZXuSkA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC_CLQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 31, "title": "Prefetch HDMA's initial descriptor and indirect address during frame initialization", "body": "## Problem

HDMA frame initialization does not prepare the first table row. At baseline `d6d878b15963e5174084473f8be5592228a1d23d`, initialization copies table addresses and clears internal counters; the first descriptor and indirect address are fetched later, alongside the first HBlank payload. Consequently, table edits between initialization and HBlank can incorrectly change the first row.

Evidence:

- [machine.rs initialization and transfer paths](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d6d878b15963e5174084473f8be5592228a1d23d/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L498) separate neither initial table fetches nor their observable register effects from the first payload.
- [Raster scheduling](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d6d878b15963e5174084473f8be5592228a1d23d/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L143) starts with initialization unset and requests it at frame wrap. Its phase must not be assumed hardware-accurate.
- [The existing DMA contention test](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d6d878b15963e5174084473f8be5592228a1d23d/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L646) manually sets `hdma_init`. The [DMA test helper](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d6d878b15963e5174084473f8be5592228a1d23d/crates/snes-core/src/machine/dma_tests.rs#L244) requests initialization and HBlank together. Neither demonstrates natural initialization followed by a separate first payload.
- [Issue #29's remaining limits](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d6d878b15963e5174084473f8be5592228a1d23d/docs/issue-29-validation.md#remaining-uncertainty-and-inventory) explicitly retain initialization, overhead and first-frame uncertainty.

This addresses the next incomplete behavior identified by the latest assessment. The supplied history lists no open Issue covering it. Issue #29 corrected reverse WMDATA conflict effects; it did not implement initialization prefetch.

## Expected outcome

Implement a distinct frame-initialization operation that prepares enabled HDMA channels before their first HBlank payload.

Use [Anomie's Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), sections **DMA AND HDMA → HDMA**, **420C HDMAEN**, and **43x0–43xA**, with [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), **DMA and HDMA Channel 0..7 Registers** and HDMA timing descriptions. The repository records the references and retrieved versions in [Issue #29's specification evidence](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d6d878b15963e5174084473f8be5592228a1d23d/docs/issue-29-validation.md#retrieved-specification-evidence).

The implementation contract is:

1. Service frame initialization once at the supported scanline-0 initialization event, separately from HBlank payload processing. Cover the initial modeled frame and subsequent frame wraps. Writing `$420C` must not manufacture an initialization event merely to make a cold-start test pass.
2. For enabled channels, initialize the table address `$43x8/$43x9` from `$43x2/$43x3`, fetch the initial line descriptor through the existing A-bus access path, and expose the fetched line state in `$43xA`. Table addressing uses `$43x4`; address increments wrap within 16 bits without carrying into the bank.
3. For a nonzero indirect row, fetch its little-endian indirect address into `$43x5/$43x6` during initialization. `$43x7` remains the separate payload bank. Direction changes payload direction, not descriptor/pointer reads.
4. Initialization performs no B-bus payload access and does not consume a scanline of the row. The first payload uses the prepared descriptor/address. Payload data remains live until its actual transfer; prefetching table metadata must not prefetch direct or indirect payload bytes.
5. A zero initial descriptor prevents payload transfer without clearing the programmed `$420C` enable bit. Implement its indirect-pointer fetch effects according to the cited specification, rather than assuming the existing early return is correct.
6. Disabled channels must not generate table reads. Preserve programmed source addresses and the established payload access restrictions and WRAM-conflict effects.

The full reference documents and their cached copies are absent from this checkout. Numeric initialization phase, overhead, enable-edge details, and indirect zero-header fetch quirks were therefore **not independently verified by this planning pass**. Resolve those narrow details against the named references before encoding their expectations. Record supported ordering separately from approximate clock alignment; existing constants and another emulator's implementation are not hardware oracles. Correct unsupported earlier test contracts when necessary.

### Scope and remaining work

Limit production changes to frame-initialization scheduling, initial metadata reads/register state, and integration with the existing HDMA/DMA event paths. Handle overlap with general DMA on another channel without losing or duplicating initialization or the first payload.

Subsequent row-reload fetch placement, complete HDMA overhead/alignment accuracy, same-channel DMA/HDMA contention, arbitrary mid-frame enabling, electrical open-bus values, PAL/interlace/overscan, and pixel-fetch timing remain separate work. Document retained approximations explicitly. This Issue does not certify the entire HDMA category.

## Context and reproduction

Build original direct and indirect tables in WRAM, configure their channels during VBlank, and advance normally into the next frame. After initialization has completed but before the first HBlank:

- Change the initial descriptor, or the indirect address bytes, to distinct alternatives.
- Separately change the selected payload byte.

Expected: the first transfer retains the initialized descriptor/address while observing the later payload-byte change. Current source predicts that it instead observes the replacement metadata because metadata reads occur at HBlank. Confirm this with executable baseline failures; this planning pass inspected source only and ran no tests.

Use safe timing margins established from the specification. Do not require a guest that enables HDMA after the initialization point to run in that same frame. Guest configuration during VBlank followed by the next frame provides a reachable setup.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record a concise source-backed initialization event/state table covering enabled-channel order, direct/indirect nonzero headers, zero headers, register effects, first payload separation, and the selected initialization timing convention. Identify unresolved subcycle details honestly; do not invent numeric guarantees.
- [ ] Implement initial metadata prefetch, rather than delivering only an audit or documentation update. Demonstrate baseline failures for metadata visibility before HBlank and metadata edits between initialization and first payload, followed by passing corrected tests.
- [ ] Add original scheduler tests driven through normal clock/event progression, without setting `hdma_init`, `hdma_pending`, or active/line state to create the event being tested. Cover initial modeled-frame scheduling, frame wrap, direct and indirect channels, zero termination, disabled-channel controls, multiple enabled channels, and table-address wrapping. Assert prepared registers before any payload occurs.
- [ ] Verify that first-row payload bytes remain live, table/pointer reads retain existing A-bus restrictions and register side effects, and initialization produces no payload-port side effects.
- [ ] Cover general DMA on a different channel crossing frame initialization and the first HBlank. Assert exactly-once initialization and payload progression, completed general-DMA address/count state, continued raster/APU advancement, and CPU suspension during the transfer.
- [ ] Add `crates/snes-core/tests/hdma_init.rs` with original source-built CPU guests for direct and indirect prefetch. Guests must configure registers, synchronize, modify table/payload bytes, and report numeric results through executed instructions. Host code supplies the cartridge and observes results without injecting private state. Bound execution by explicit instruction/frame limits. Record original MIT code/data/header provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Preserve existing DMA/HDMA payload, restriction, reverse-conflict, refresh, NMI and contention regressions. Update expectations affected by corrected initialization only with documented independent justification; do not retain a contradicted hardware contract merely to preserve a passing assertion.
- [ ] Pass the following pre-merge commands using the README's supported toolchain selection where needed:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib machine::
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dma_access
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test hdma_init
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

- [ ] Preserve pinned source inputs, licensing decisions, fixture assertions and existing Castle/Memory gameplay, audio, duration and route checks. The licensed HDMA fixture must retain its eleven grayscale bands through line 223. Report actual commands/results and any failures or skipped checks in the PR validation record; mandatory checks must pass before merge. See [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d6d878b15963e5174084473f8be5592228a1d23d/README.md#validate).
- [ ] Update README limits and the validation record to distinguish the implemented prefetch behavior from remaining HDMA work. Limited test passes establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

All 24 inventory scopes remain intact: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, and `dsp-timing` remain partial; `dsp-voices` remains implemented_unverified; `ppu-hires`, `ppu-raster`, and `pal` remain unimplemented. Completion improves the selected HDMA behavior without verifying untouched scopes.
